issues.description: Command names break the codebase's singular-dash convention (quickmarks-reload vs quickmark-save).
issues.detail: New commands are registered as quickmarks_reload / bookmarks_reload (exposed as :quickmarks-reload / :bookmarks-reload), but every sibling command uses singular form: quickmark-add, quickmark-save, bookmark-add. Pick one convention and match the surrounding code, or justify the break in the commit message. Feature tests also use the plural form, propagating the inconsistency.

issues.description: reload() is not atomic and silently discards unsaved in-memory state.
issues.detail: reload() calls self.marks.clear() then re-parses; a parse failure leaves marks empty rather than preserving the previous state. It also blows away any in-memory changes not yet flushed by save-manager, with no docstring note. Build the new OrderedDict locally and swap on success, and document the discard-unsaved contract.

issues.description: Feature file scenarios are unnamed, breaking the file's voice.
issues.detail: Both new Gherkin scenarios start with bare 'Scenario:' with no title. Every other scenario in the file has a descriptive name ('Saving a quickmark', etc.). Cheap fix; helps test output stay greppable and readable in reports.

issues.description: Unit test coverage is thin — doesn't verify the clear-on-reload contract or pre-reload state.
issues.detail: test_reload only checks the happy-path replacement case. It does not assert that entries removed from disk are dropped on reload, does not verify the pre-reload marks were actually loaded by __init__, and does not exercise a malformed-file reload (where the atomicity concern surfaces). A couple more assertions would lock the contract.

issues.description: Two near-identical command bodies invite a small helper.
issues.detail: quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload are six lines each, identical except for the registry key and message string. Not worth a hierarchy, but a small _reload_marks(name, label) helper would make the duplication explicit. Optional — duplication this small is also fine to leave.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the refactor extracting reload() from __init__ is the right shape — one code path owns mark loading, used at both construction and refresh. The dominant concern is command naming: quickmarks-reload / bookmarks-reload break the existing singular-dash convention (quickmark-save, bookmark-add) and should be renamed or justified. Secondary issues cluster around reload()'s lack of atomicity and undocumented discard of unsaved state, thin unit-test coverage of the clear-on-reload contract, and unnamed Gherkin scenarios that break the feature file's voice. No blockers; ship after the naming fix and a few small cleanups.
